name: How do I finance a whole-house remodel in Southern California?

mainEntity.name: What are the common ways homeowners pay for a large remodel when the budget is six figures?
mainEntity.text: What are the common ways homeowners pay for a large remodel when the budget is six figures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Large whole-house remodels often require a financing plan before work begins. Many homeowners use savings combined with home equity, a home equity line of credit, a renovation loan, or a cash-out refinance. More complex projects may require construction-style financing, especially if the remodel is extensive or paired with an addition. The right option depends on how much equity is available, how quickly funds are needed, and whether the loan needs to cover design, permits, and construction in stages. It also matters whether the homeowner plans to occupy the home during work or move out temporarily. Before committing, homeowners should compare payment timing, interest costs, and flexibility for change orders. A realistic financing plan should leave room for contingencies, not just the initial bid. That protects the project if hidden issues or scope changes arise mid-construction.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common financing options include savings, home equity lines of credit, renovation loans, cash-out refinancing, and construction loans. The right choice depends on equity, interest rates, timeline, and whether the project will be done in one phase or multiple phases.
